title: Reflux Esophagitis (the Gulpies)
desc: Gulping and repeated swallowing in dogs — omeprazole, metoclopramide and sucralfate, with the meal-timing routine that makes or breaks the response.

meds.name: Omeprazole
meds.desc: reduces stomach acid so the refluxed fluid stops burning
freqs: twice daily, 30 minutes before a meal
meds.note: 1 mg/kg PO q 12 h. Timing matters: give each dose 30 minutes BEFORE a meal. If the episodes are worse overnight, give the second dose at BEDTIME rather than at dinner.

meds.name: Metoclopramide
meds.desc: tightens the lower esophageal sphincter and moves the stomach along
freqs: every 8–12 hours, 30 minutes before a meal
meds.note: 0.2–0.4 mg/kg PO q 8–12 h, each dose 30 minutes before a meal and again at bedtime. After the bedtime dose give a small meal 30 minutes later, then it really is bedtime.

meds.name: Sucralfate
meds.doseText: ½ to 1 tablet (1 g tablets) as a water slurry
meds.note: Give as a slurry in water, on an empty stomach, an hour or more apart from meals and from any other medication — it will bind the other drugs otherwise.

meds.grp: If inflammatory bowel disease is also present
meds.name: Prednisolone
meds.desc: anti-inflammatory, if IBD is part of the picture
meds.doseText: prednisolone at your usual IBD dose
meds.note: Listed on the source sheet as an option only where IBD is present, without a dose. Choose the dose from your usual IBD protocol.

meds.grp: If inflammatory bowel disease is also present
meds.name: Budesonide
meds.doseText: budesonide at your usual IBD dose
meds.note: Listed on the source sheet as an option for concurrent IBD, without a dose.

meds.grp: If inflammatory bowel disease is also present
meds.name: Cyclosporine

notes.The pattern to look for: Repeated gulping, licking, or swallowing — often in bouts, often worse at night or on an empty stomach. It frequently looks far more dramatic on video than on examination.
notes.How fast you will know: If reflux is the right idea this works immediately — usually within a week you can tell whether the pattern has been interrupted, depending on how often the episodes were happening.
notes.Timing is the treatment: The drugs do little if the timing is wrong. Both omeprazole and metoclopramide go in 30 minutes before food; a small meal at bedtime keeps the stomach from being empty overnight.
notes.Worked example from the sheet: A dog on omeprazole 30 mg BID and metoclopramide 10 mg BID–TID, each dose 30 minutes before a meal and again at bedtime.

dischargeBlocks.title: What is going on
dischargeBlocks.text: The gulping, licking and repeated swallowing you are seeing is almost certainly acid coming back up into {name}'s food pipe. It is uncomfortable rather than dangerous, and it usually settles quickly once we interrupt the pattern.

dischargeBlocks.title: When to give the medication — this is the important part
dischargeBlocks.text:
These medicines only work properly if they go in at the right time.

- Give each dose 30 minutes BEFORE a meal, not with food.
- Give the evening dose at bedtime rather than at dinner if the episodes are worse overnight.
- After the bedtime dose, wait 30 minutes and give a small meal, then settle {name} for the night.

An empty stomach overnight is what sets off most of these episodes.

dischargeBlocks.title: If we sent home sucralfate (Carafate)
dischargeBlocks.text:
Crush the tablet and mix it with a little water into a slurry, then give it.

- Give it on an empty stomach.
- Keep it at least one hour away from meals and from every other medication — it will stick to the other drugs and stop them working.

dischargeBlocks.title: What to expect
dischargeBlocks.text:
If we have the right idea, this works quickly. You should be able to tell within about a week whether the episodes are settling.

Please keep a rough note of how often the gulping happens so we can compare.

dischargeBlocks.title: Follow up
dischargeBlocks.text: Please let us know in about a week how {name} is doing. If there is no change at all, call us — it may not be reflux, and we will want to look further.
